1840.s: On her head she wore a full frizzed, yet small red peruke, elaborately studded with very costly pearls, rubies, and diamonds.

“But we, ” said Marguerite, “belong, in every respect, to the century of frizzed and powdered wigs, the time of the late Louis le Grand ; we shall, therefore, always remain a century apart; and while you are rejoicing in your prime, we shall appear before the eyes of wisdom, like the prophetic shadows of a future…

1860.s: Her thin face, her hooked nose, her little frizzed yellow wig, and her long waist — for she was dressed in the style of my grandmother — made such a queer figure that I could scarcely refrain from laughing.

1900.s: …but, as I say, the impression which she conveyed was solely one of great age, and this — far from being reduced — was thrown into a high and even mocking light by the fact that she wore a crooked, frizzed, brown little wig under her jaunty lace cap, and that upon those wrinkled cheeks there was a lavish display of rouge.
